title: Ampleness is invariant under isomorphisms of invertible modules
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and L and N invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] on X. If L and N are isomorphic as O_X-modules, then L is ample if and only if N is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Definition 01PS and Section 01PR; section-transport argument in Proposition 09NZ of varieties.tex, second sentence

proof.text: Construct tensorPow_iso by induction on n using Scheme.Modules.tensorPow from the source Invertible module: degree zero uses Iso.refl of the monoidal unit, and the successor uses the monoidal tensor of the given isomorphism with the induction isomorphism. No positiveTensorPower or change-of-rings construction is used.

Prove stalk_map_smul for the commutative-ring-valued scheme stalk. Represent both the scalar and vector as germs using TopCat.Presheaf.exists_germ_eq, restrict to the intersection of their neighborhoods with germ_res_apply, and apply PresheafOfModules.germ_smul, stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply, and Hom.app_smul. This gives linearity over X.presheaf.stalk x without using the ring-valued moduleStalkFunctor.

For any module isomorphism, apply toPresheaf followed by the abelian-group stalk functor. Its hom and inv are additive inverse stalk maps, and stalk_map_smul makes them linear over the commutative stalk ring. Mathlib Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top shows that each map preserves the maximal ideal times the whole stalk. The inverse identity gives the converse membership implication. Compatibility with germs then proves nonvanishingLocus_iso for the transported global section.

Unpack IsAmple. Preserve CompactSpace X and, for each point, its positive exponent and affine open. Transport the witnessing section along tensorPow_iso; nonvanishingLocus_iso identifies the required pointwise predicates. Apply the same construction to the inverse isomorphism for the reverse implication. On the empty scheme the pointwise obligation is vacuous.
